Class InputAction

Namespace
ShapeEngine.Input
Assembly
ShapeEngine.dll

Represents an input action, which can be triggered by various input types and devices. Handles state, multi-tap, hold, and axis sensitivity/gravity.

Fields

BlocksInput

Gets or sets whether this input action blocks input types after use. InputAction has to be part of an InputActionTree to participate in the blocking system.

If set to true, input types used by this action will be added to the block list for the current frame, preventing other actions from using the same input types until the next frame.

If Active is set to false, or if AccessTag does not have access, this action will not block input types. 

public bool BlocksInput

Field Value

bool

Remarks

Only InputActions with BlocksInput enabled participate in this blocking system. If set to false, this action neither blocks input types nor can it be blocked by others.

Properties

AccessTag

The access tag used for locking/unlocking this action.

  • Determines access of this action.
  • Only used when input actions are locked.
  • If this tag is contained in the lock blacklist while the lock is active, the InputState of this InputAction will not be available.
  • If this tag is contained in the lock whitelist while the lock is active, the InputState of this InputAction will always be available.
  • If AllAccessTag is used the InputState of this InputAction will always be available, regardless of the lock state.
public uint AccessTag { get; }

Property Value

uint

Active

Indicates if this input action is active. If set to false, the action will not process input or update its state.

ExecutionOrder

Gets or sets the execution order for this InputAction.

Input actions with a lower ExecutionOrder value are processed first.

This value is automatically assigned when the action is created, but can be set manually if needed.

This only has an effect when used with InputActionTree or in other sorted collections that use CompareTo(InputAction?) for determining order.

public int ExecutionOrder { get; set; }

Property Value

int

Remarks

If two InputAction have the same ExecutionOrder, Id is used to determine the order. A lower Id value is processed first.

This is especially useful when combined with BlocksInput, as it allows precise control over which InputAction instances can block others based on their execution order.

Consume(out bool)

Consumes the current input State and marks it as consumed.

public InputState Consume(out bool valid)

Parameters

valid bool

True if the state was not already consumed; otherwise, false.

Returns

InputState

The previous input state before consumption.

Remarks

Useful for InputAction instances that may be referenced in multiple places, but should only be consumed once per frame. For example, a "menu accept" action might be used in several contexts, but should only trigger in the first context that processes it. If your system ensures single-use per frame by design, this method is unnecessary. InputActionTrees are helpful for isolating input actions, allowing only one tree to be active at a time.

Copy()

Creates a deep of copy of this InputAction, including deep copies of all associated IInputTypes. A new ID is generated for the copy and the Parent is not set, as the copy should not be part of the same tree as the original.

Update(float, out InputDeviceType)

Updates the input action state when it is not part of an InputActionTree. This method should only be used for standalone actions. If the action is in a tree, the update is skipped, because the InputActionTree will handle the update automatically.

public bool Update(float dt, out InputDeviceType inputDeviceType)

Parameters

dt float

The time delta in seconds.

inputDeviceType InputDeviceType

Outputs the detected input device type.

Returns

bool

true if the action was updated; otherwise, false.

Remarks

Because the InputAction is not part of an InputActionTree, the IInputType Block system is not used.
